title: Case study landing page layout + PDF template system
creator: Ben Carter
description:
Context
We’re launching the structured case study + customer reference program (3–5 initial stories). Design needs to provide (1) a web case study page layout that works inside redwood-docs and (2) a reusable PDF template system for downloadable one-pagers / full case study PDFs.

Goals
- Web: create a consistent, scannable case study page that highlights measurable outcomes (latency/cost/reliability) + deployment mode (Hosted/Dedicated/Private), with room for technical depth (architecture + implementation).
- PDF: create a template system that can be produced quickly (Marketing) and looks consistent across stories, with strong typography + accessibility.
- Ensure both web + PDF support the “production economics” messaging (latency, cost/token, reliability, deployment flexibility) without encouraging risky/over-specific security claims.

Non-goals
- Full site redesign beyond the case studies section.
- New brand work; use existing Redwood visual system.

Deliverables
1) Web case study templates (desktop + mobile)
A. Case study index/list page
- Header: “Customer stories” with short positioning line (production-grade inference outcomes)
- Optional filters/tags (phase 2; design now with future slot): Deployment mode, Industry, Workload type (chat/embeddings/rerank), Region
- Cards: Customer logo (or anonymized placeholder), 1-line summary, 2–3 headline metrics, deployment badge (Hosted/Dedicated/Private), “Read story” CTA
- Empty states: no stories / no matches

B. Case study detail page (core)
- Hero
  - Customer name + short descriptor (e.g., “Regulated healthcare platform running in VPC”) OR anonymized label (e.g., “US Healthcare Platform (Anonymized)”)
  - Deployment badge (Hosted / Dedicated / Private)
  - 2–4 verified outcomes as metric chips (e.g., “p95 latency ↓ 38%”, “cost/query ↓ 27%”, “error rate ↓ 60%”, “time-to-production 6 weeks → 10 days”)
  - Proof note pattern: small caption “Metrics measured over [window], workload-specific” (ties to metrics validation process)
- Problem + constraints section
  - Bulleted constraints block (security/compliance, traffic shape, SLOs)
- Architecture section
  - Architecture diagram slot (SVG/PNG) with caption + alt text requirement
  - “Key components” list (runtime, routing/fallback, caching/batching, Dedicated/Private specifics)
- Implementation section
  - Steps / timeline; optional callout boxes for “What surprised us” / “Operational learnings”
- Outcomes section
  - Before/after table pattern for latency/cost/reliability (with caveat footnotes)
  - Optional charts (simple) with accessible labeling
- Quote section
  - Pull quote with attribution; supports “Approved quote only” note for internal drafts
- Security & compliance (conditional)
  - If present, use a standardized pattern: “Security considerations” with non-sensitive wording + link to Redwood security docs; avoid publishing architecture details like subnet names, vendors, or internal system names
- Final CTA
  - “Talk to us” / “See docs” + “Request a reference call” (internal link gated as needed)
- Print-friendly styling (CSS) to support browser print and PDF export fallback

2) PDF template system (Google Docs → PDF or Figma → PDF)
- Two formats:
  - 1-page reference sheet (exec-friendly)
  - 4–6 page full case study (mirrors web narrative)
- Template components
  - Cover header with logo, title, customer descriptor, deployment badge
  - Metric tiles (2–4)
  - Problem/Constraints block
  - Architecture diagram page/section
  - Outcomes table + footnotes pattern for measurement windows
  - Quote component
  - CTA / contact block + legal footer line
- Export requirements
  - Must export to tagged PDF where feasible; otherwise ensure readable structure (heading hierarchy, selectable text, high contrast)
  - Consistent page margins; no critical info in bleed/trim risk areas

Typography + layout guidance (web + PDF)
- Use existing Redwood docs typography tokens where possible
- Heading hierarchy must be strictly H1 → H2 → H3 (no skipped levels)
- Default line length targets: 65–80 characters on web body
- Metric chips: use tabular numerals if available; ensure units are explicit (ms, $, %, tokens)
- Diagram captions: minimum 12–14px equivalent and meet contrast requirements

Accessibility requirements (must-haves)
- WCAG 2.1 AA contrast for all text and UI components
- Keyboard focus visible for interactive elements (index filters, TOC anchors, CTAs)
- Provide alt text for all diagrams/images; for complex diagrams include a “Text description” collapsible block on web
- Avoid color-only encoding for deployment mode badges; include text label
- Responsive behavior: no horizontal scroll on mobile; tables must have a mobile pattern (stacked rows or scroll with clear affordance)

Engineering handoff expectations
- Provide component specs + spacing tokens for:
  - Metric chips / tiles
  - Callout blocks
  - Outcomes table
  - Quote block
  - Deployment badge
  - Diagram figure + caption
- Provide a minimal style guide for case studies in docs: typography, max image width, recommended diagram background, code snippet styling if used.

Open questions
- Final system for PDF generation: Marketing prefers Google Docs for speed, Design prefers Figma for fidelity. Proposal: master in Figma (source of truth), with a simplified Google Docs version for quick-turn drafts; align with Camila/Soojin.
- Case study index filters: ship without filters in v1 (ENG scope) but reserve UI space; confirm with Ben/ENG-4921.

Links / artifacts
- Figma (working): https://figma.com/file/REDACTED/DES-214-Case-Studies (internal)
- Messaging framework: https://confluence.redwoodinference.com/display/PMM/Case+Study+Messaging+Framework+-+Production+Economics
- Engineering implementation ticket: ENG-4921 (case-studies section in redwood-docs)
- Program launch ticket: PM-684

Acceptance criteria
- [ ] Figma includes: index page + detail page (desktop/mobile) + component variants
- [ ] PDF templates delivered (1-page + multi-page) with editable text styles and consistent spacing
- [ ] A11y checklist completed (contrast, focus, headings, alt text guidance)
- [ ] Handoff notes posted for ENG (component specs + responsive behaviors)
- [ ] Quick review with PMM + Legal on “safe to publish” diagram/detail guidance
comments: 2025-05-10 (Ben Carter): Creating design ticket to unblock docs implementation. We need a template that’s strong enough for Arcadia/QuantaPay/NovaDocs but flexible for anonymized stories.
2025-05-13 (Soojin Lee): Please ensure outcomes callouts have room for caveats (measurement window, workload). We’ve had redlines on absolute claims like “2x faster” without context.

2025-05-15 (Tessa Morgan): First pass wireframes in Figma: index cards with metric chips + deployment badge. Detail page uses modular blocks so we can omit sections (e.g., Security) per customer approval.

2025-05-18 (Markus Klein): Architecture section needs to support both ‘simple’ and ‘deep’ diagrams. Some customers will only allow a high-level box diagram; others may allow components like routing/fallback and cache layers. Design should handle both without looking empty.
2025-05-21 (Camila Reyes): PDF is critical for sales follow-up. Request: 1-page version that Sales can attach immediately after a reference call + longer version for website download.
2025-05-24 (Ben Carter): ENG-4921 will likely ship v1 without filters. Please keep index layout that works without filters and can accept them later.
2025-05-27 (Tessa Morgan): Added a11y notes to Figma and proposed ‘Text description’ block for complex diagrams. Also added print-friendly spacing rules for tables and quote blocks.

2025-06-02 (Naomi Feldman): Reminder: do not imply compliance certifications on customer pages unless explicitly approved. Security section should link to Redwood security docs rather than restating certification language in the case study body.

2025-06-04 (Tessa Morgan): Marking In Review. Ready for PMM/Eng review: component specs + responsive behaviors documented on Figma page ‘Handoff’. Pending decision on PDF source-of-truth (Figma vs Google Docs).
